mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days without regime dependency.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate decline below 0.25% for two consecutive months signals aggressive monetary policy intervention during economic distress, triggering positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered instances, or Rank IC remains negative over any 1-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in consumer credit (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) signal deepening private sector demand contraction, prompting policy responses that drive positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The RSAFS-HOUST interaction fails to produce positive 60-day returns in at least 60% of cases, or interaction term Rank IC is below 0.01.

mechanism_narrative: In high-unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 9.5%), a monthly unemployment rate decline exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals labor market stabilization, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 9.5% and UNRATE decline > 0.5pp in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered instances, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 in high-unemployment periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained industrial production decline below 90 for two consecutive months indicates manufacturing sector weakness, triggering policy support that produces positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is below 90 for two consecutive months, or Rank IC is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) remains below 0.5% for two consecutive quarters, it signals weak economic recovery, prompting stimulus that drives positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth < 0.5% for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered instances, or Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 1-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous employment decline (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate rise (UNRATE) signal labor market deterioration, triggering short-term equity rebounds within 5 trading days as policy intervention is anticipated.
failure_condition: The PAYEMS-UNRATE interaction fails to produce positive 5-day returns in at least 60% of cases, or interaction term Rank IC is below 0.01.

mechanism_narrative: In post-recession expansions (GDP growth > 1.0% for two consecutive quarters), a consumer credit (RSAFS) rise above its 12-month moving average signals strengthening demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 1.0% for 2 consecutive quarters and RSAFS > 12-month moving average
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered instances, or Rank IC for RSAFS above 12-month MA in post-recession regime is below 0.02.
